| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ὣς φάτο, τῷ δ’ ἔμπνευσε μένος γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη (10.482, whole-line formula) | "So he spoke, and in him breathed might gleaming-eyed Athena," | "So he spoke, and gleaming-eyed Athena breathed might into Diomedes," | "inspired", "put strength into" (ἐμπνέω is "breathe into" and μένος "might"); γλαυκῶπις keeps the Odyssey’s "gleaming-eyed"; ὣς φάτο is "So he spoke" |
| ἐπιστροφάδην (10.483) | "turning this way and that" | "turning this way and that" | "right and left", "in a whirl", "in a circle" (each picks a sense); built on ἐπιστρέφω "turn about", rare word |
| ἀσημάντοισιν (μήλοισιν, 10.485) | "unguarded" | "unguarded" (+ note: literally "unmarked"; sense not certain) | "unshepherded" (decides the guess), "unmarked", "with no signal" |
| κύντατον (10.503; superlative of κύων) | "most dog-like" | "most shameless" | "boldest", "most daring", "bravest" (each drops the dog and picks a sense in `i`); follows the Odyssey table’s κύντερον "more dog-like" / "more shameless" |
| Οἰνεΐδαο πάϊς (10.497) | "the child of Oeneus’ son" | "the child of Oeneus’ son" | "Diomedes" (names what the Greek leaves for the note), "grandson of Oeneus"; Οἰνεΐδης is Tydeus, as the iliad-034 unit at 5.812 has "the son of Oeneus" |
| διὰ μῆτιν Ἀθήνης (10.497) | "through the cunning of Athena" | "by the cunning of Athena" | "plan", "design" (reserved for βουλή), "counsel"; μῆτις keeps "cunning" (Odyssey table) |
| ῥοίζησεν (10.502) | "he whistled" | "he whistled" | "hissed", "whizzed" (the word is also used of missiles), "made a sound"; the signal is a whistle |
| πιφαύσκων (10.502) | "making it known" | "to signal" | "showing", "telling" (the Greek gives no object; "signal" supplies the sense of the act); the verb is πιφαύσκω "make known" as in iliad-062 |
| ἀήθεσσον (10.493) | "were unused to" | "were still unused to" | "were not accustomed to", "feared"; ἀηθέω "be unused to", genitive of the thing |
| ὑψόσ’ ἀείρας (10.505) | "lifting it up high" | "lift it high" | follows the iliad-062 unit at 10.465 ("raising the spoils high") |
| ἀνεψιὸν ἐσθλόν (10.519) | "a good cousin" | "a good cousin" | "noble cousin", "brave kinsman"; ἐσθλός keeps "good"; ἀνεψιός "cousin" as in "kinsmen and cousins" (9.464) |
| ὦρσεν … βουληφόρον (10.518) | "he roused … the counsel-bearer" | "roused … a counsellor of the Thracians" | follows the table’s βουληφόρος "counsel-bearer" / "counsellor" (7.126) |
| ἀσπαίροντας ἐν ἀργαλέῃσι φονῇσιν (10.521) | "gasping in grievous slaughter" | "gasping in grievous slaughter" | "grievous deaths", "bloody pools" (φονή is "slaughter", plural dative); ἀργαλέος keeps the Odyssey’s "grievous"; ἀσπαίρω keeps "gasping" (3.293) |
| ᾤμωξέν τ’ … φίλον τ’ ὀνόμηνεν ἑταῖρον (10.522) | "and he cried out … and named his dear companion" | "he cried out, and called his dear companion by name" | "groaned" (reserved for στενάχω / στόνος), "wailed"; ᾤμωξεν keeps "cried out" (Odyssey 13.198, odyssey-063); ὀνομαίνω "name", "call by name" |
| θηεῦντο (10.524) | "they gazed at" | "they gazed at" | "marvelled at", "looked on"; θηέομαι "gaze at" |
| ὅσσ’ ἄνδρες ῥέξαντες ἔβαν (10.525) | "all that the men had done before they went" | "all that the men had done before going off" | "all the men had done in leaving", "wrought"; ῥέζω "do", ἔβαν "went" |
| σκοπὸν Ἕκτορος ἔκταν (10.526) | "Hector’s scout they had killed" | "Hector’s scout" | "spy" (reserved for διοπτήρ, 10.562), "lookout"; σκοπός keeps "scout" (iliad-058, ἐπίσκοπον "as a scout") |
| νῆας ἔπι γλαφυράς · τῇ γὰρ φίλον ἔπλετο θυμῷ (10.531) | "to the hollow ships" · "for thither it was dear to their spirit" | "to the hollow ships" · "for it pleased their spirit to go that way" | "for that was where their spirit wanted to go" (drops φίλον), "for so it was dear to their spirit" (τῇ read as "so"); the line follows iliad-041’s ὣς φίλον ἔπλετο θυμῷ "so it has been dear to the spirit", with τῇ as "thither" |
| Νέστωρ δὲ πρῶτος κτύπον ἄϊε φώνησέν τε (10.532, whole-line speech introduction) | "And Nestor first heard the thud, and spoke:" | "Nestor was the first to hear the thud, and he spoke:" | "din", "clatter", "noise" (κτύπος is a beating or thud; ὀρυμαγδός keeps "din"), "cried out"; φώνησεν keeps "spoke" (iliad-004, -018, -034) |
| ἵππων μ’ ὠκυπόδων ἀμφὶ κτύπος οὔατα βάλλει (10.535) | "Of horses swift-footed the thud around strikes my ears." | "The thud of swift-footed horses is beating around my ears." | "rings in my ears", "falls on my ears"; ὠκύπους keeps "swift-footed" (5.296) |
| αἲ γὰρ δὴ … ἐλασαίατο (10.536–537) | "If only … might drive off" | "If only … might drive … off" | "would that", "I wish"; ἐλαύνω middle "drive off" |
| ὑπὸ Τρώων ὀρυμαγδοῦ (10.539) | "under the din of the Trojans" | "in the Trojans’ din" | "at the hands of the Trojans’ din", "from the Trojan uproar"; ὀρυμαγδός keeps "din" (iliad-015, -025, -046) |
| οὔ πω πᾶν εἴρητο ἔπος ὅτ’ ἄρ’ ἤλυθον αὐτοί (10.540) | "Not yet the whole word had been spoken, when they themselves came." | "He had not yet finished speaking when they themselves arrived." | follows Odyssey 16.11 (odyssey-077), οὔ πω πᾶν εἴρητο ἔπος, ὅτε …; the tail differs, so this is not a repeated line |
| δεξιῇ ἠσπάζοντο ἔπεσσί τε μειλιχίοισι (10.542) | "with the right hand greeted them, and with words gentle" | "greeted them with their right hands and with gentle words" | "welcomed", "embraced"; follows Odyssey 19.415 (χερσίν τ’ ἠσπάζοντο …) with the hand singular |
| πρῶτος δ’ ἐξερέεινε Γερήνιος ἱππότα Νέστωρ (10.543, whole-line speech introduction) | "and first questioned them the Gerenian horseman Nestor:" | "And first the Gerenian horseman Nestor questioned them:" | "interrogated", "asked"; ἐξερεείνω keeps "question" (iliad-057, -058) and "Gerenian horseman" the table’s 7.170 |
| αἰνῶς ἀκτίνεσσιν ἐοικότες ἠελίοιο (10.547) | "Dreadfully like the rays of the sun." | "Dreadfully like the rays of the sun." | "strikingly" (drops αἰνῶς), "terribly like", "wonderfully", "marvellously"; follows the table’s αἰνῶς … ἔοικεν (3.158) "dreadfully … is like" in both layers |
| μιμνάζειν (10.549) · ἐπιμίσγομαι (10.548) | "linger" · "mingle with" | "linger" · "mingle with" | "hang back", "stay" (`i` keeps "linger"); ἐπιμίσγομαι keeps the Odyssey’s "mingles" (odyssey-028, odyssey-029) |
| οὐδέ τί φημι μιμνάζειν (10.548–549) | "in no way do I say that I linger" | "I deny that I linger" | "I do not claim to"; φημί with a negated infinitive is "deny" in `i` only |
| ἴδον οὐδὲ νόησα (10.550) | "seen or noticed" | "seen or taken note of" | "perceived", "marked"; νοέω "notice, take note of" |
| ὔμμ’ ὀΐω δόμεναι θεὸν ἀντιάσαντα (10.551) | "I think some god, having met you, gave them to you" | "I think some god met you and gave them to you" | "I suppose", "I believe"; ὀΐω "I think", ἀντιάω "meet" (iliad-001, -036, -043) |
| ῥεῖα θεός γ’ ἐθέλων … δωρήσαιτ’ (10.556–557) | "easily a god, if willing, … could give" | "a god, if he wished, could easily give" | follows Odyssey 3.231 (odyssey-011): ῥεῖα θεός γ’ ἐθέλων "easily a god, if willing" / "a god, if willing, could easily" |
| ἐπεὶ ἢ πολὺ φέρτεροί εἰσιν (10.557, the gods as subject) | "since indeed they are much stronger" | "since the gods are far stronger" | "better" (the Odyssey ships "by far better" at 16.89, odyssey-077; here "stronger", as at 9.276 odyssey-041); the note says "they" are the gods |
| ἵπποι … νεήλυδες … Θρηΐκιοι (10.558–559) | "newcomers … Thracian ones" | "newcomers, and Thracian" | "newly arrived", "newly come"; νεήλυς keeps "newcomer(s)" (iliad-062, 10.433) |
| ἀγαθὸς Διομήδης (10.559) | "good Diomedes" | "Good Diomedes" | "brave", "valiant" (reserved for ἄλκιμος), "excellent"; ἀγαθός without βοήν is plain "good"; κρατερός Διομήδης keeps "strong" |
| τὸν τρισκαιδέκατον σκοπὸν εἵλομεν (10.561) | "as the thirteenth the scout we took" | "as the thirteenth we caught a scout" | "seized", "captured"; αἱρέω "take", "catch" in `i` |
| διοπτῆρα στρατοῦ ἔμμεναι ἡμετέροιο (10.562) | "to be a spy of our army" | "to spy on our army" | "watcher", "observer", "lookout" (reserved for σκοπός); διοπτήρ is "one who looks through", a spy |
| ὣς εἰπὼν τάφροιο διήλασε μώνυχας ἵππους καγχαλόων (10.564–565) | "So having spoken, across the ditch he drove the solid-hoofed horses, exulting;" | "So saying, he drove the solid-hoofed horses across the ditch, exulting;" | "through the ditch" (the genitive is "across"), "laughing"; καγχαλάω "exult" (iliad-016, -040) |
| κλισίην εὔτυκτον (10.566) | "well-made hut" | "well-made hut" | "well-built", "comfortable"; εὔτυκτος keeps "well-made" (8.43) |
| ἐϋτμήτοισιν ἱμᾶσι (10.567) | "well-cut straps" | "well-cut straps" | "finely cut", "well-trimmed"; keeps iliad-044’s ἐϋτμήτῳ τελαμῶνι "well-cut strap" |
| φάτνῃ ἐφ’ ἱππείῃ (10.568) | "at the horses’ manger" | "at the horses’ manger" | "stable", "stall"; φάτνη "manger" as in iliad-029, -040 |
| μελιηδέα πυρὸν ἔδοντες (10.569) | "eating honey-sweet wheat" | "eating honey-sweet wheat" | "sweet grain", "barley"; μελιηδής keeps "honey-sweet" (Odyssey table); πυρός "wheat" (iliad-047, odyssey-097) |
| ὄφρ’ ἱρὸν ἑτοιμασσαίατ’ Ἀθήνῃ (10.571) | "until they should prepare a holy offering for Athena" | "until they could prepare a sacrifice for Athena" | "so that they might", "temple", "holy rite"; ἱρόν is Ionic ἱερόν used as a noun; ἑτοιμάζω "prepare" |
| ἱδρῶ πολλὸν ἀπενίζοντο θαλάσσῃ (10.572) | "the much sweat washed off in the sea" | "washed the great sweat off" | "plenty of sweat", "dripping sweat"; ἀπονίζω "wash off", ἱδρώς "sweat" |
| κνήμας τε ἰδὲ λόφον ἀμφί τε μηρούς (10.573) | "from the shins and the neck and about the thighs" | "their shins, their necks and their thighs" | "back", "ridge", "crest" (λόφος has other senses; here the nape or neck), "calves"; κνήμη "shin" |
| ἀνέψυχθεν φίλον ἦτορ (10.575) | "their dear heart had cooled again" | "their hearts were refreshed" | "were calmed", "revived"; ἀναψύχω "cool again"; φίλον ἦτορ keeps "dear heart" (iliad-030) |
| ἔς ῥ’ ἀσαμίνθους βάντες ἐϋξέστας λούσαντο (10.576) | "into well-smoothed bathing-tubs they stepped, and washed." | "they stepped into well-polished bathing-tubs and washed." | the Odyssey’s English for the same line (4.48, odyssey-014), unchanged |
| λοεσσαμένω καὶ ἀλειψαμένω λίπ’ ἐλαίῳ (10.577) | "having washed and anointed themselves richly with olive oil" | "washed and richly anointed with olive oil" | "bathed", "rubbed with oil"; λοέω "wash", ἀλείφω "anoint", λίπα "richly" (Odyssey 6.227), ἔλαιον "olive oil" (2.754) |
| δείπνῳ ἐφιζανέτην (10.578) | "sat down to their meal" | "sat down to their meal" | "dinner", "supper" (the table keeps δεῖπνον "meal"); ἐφιζάνω "sit down at" |
| ἀπὸ δὲ κρητῆρος … πλείου ἀφυσσόμενοι λεῖβον μελιηδέα οἶνον (10.578–579) | "from the mixing-bowl … drawing from the full one, they poured honey-sweet wine" | "drawing honey-sweet wine from a full mixing-bowl, they poured a libation to Athena" | "poured out wine" (loses the libation), "drank"; λείβω "pour a libation" (Odyssey 8.430), κρητήρ "mixing-bowl", μελιηδής "honey-sweet" |
